title: Give --deviation its three required parts and a closed kind set, enforced only while armed
action: Narrow the free-form one-line --deviation value (decision dc6a2d26) to D5's three required parts — what was done differently, why, and which kind — with kind drawn from the closed set: hit an unforeseen obstacle / found a better route / the plan was wrong about a fact / something else had to be fixed first. A cap in an ARMED run must state a departure or state explicitly that the plan was followed; silence and nothing-happened must not read alike (D5). D10 bounds the enforcement: a cap in a run that files no letter keeps the byte-identical flagless behaviour dc6a2d26 promised, so an unarmed cap is unchanged. The letter renders departures through the existing knowledge::deviation_text, never a second renderer.

truths: A --deviation value carries three required parts: what was done differently, why, and which kind (D5).
The kind comes from the closed four-value set and a value outside it is refused (D5).
A cap in an ARMED run that states neither a departure nor its absence is refused (D5).
A cap that followed its plan states that explicitly rather than leaving the field empty — silence and nothing-happened do not read alike (D5).
A cap in an UNARMED run is byte-identical to today, including a bare flagless finish (D10, dc6a2d26).
Departures render through the existing knowledge::deviation_text; no second renderer is introduced.
Existing finish tests pass UNCHANGED — editing one to make it pass is a [BLOCKED], not a fix.

acceptance: The deviation flag takes three parts with a closed kind set; an armed cap must speak, an unarmed cap is unchanged; departures render through the one existing renderer; the demo in plan.md — a cap with a departure and one without, in both armed and unarmed runs — reads correctly in all four combinations.
